nodes.title: SG-3.2 Input layer module for pointer and keyboard
nodes.body:
Context: BootScene.onKeyDown and the SceneObject callbacks in BootScene.create hold the keyboard, hover and click logic inline (BootScene.ts L100-L192). Desired behavior: a new module game/frontend/src/phaser/input.ts owns object focus, moveFocus, hover, click and keyboard interaction, and emits only through phaserToReact from events.ts. Expected result: the module exists with unit tests against a mocked Phaser input plugin. Why: SG-3.3 can then switch BootScene to it. BootScene is not changed in this intent.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given objects and a keyboard plugin, when createInputLayer is called, then it registers one keydown listener and returns an InputLayer with moveFocus, focusObject, focusedId and destroy
- Given the layer, when focus moves, Enter/Space is pressed, Escape is pressed, an object is hovered or clicked, then the matching typed bridge event is emitted
- Given destroy() is called, then the keydown listener is removed and later key, hover and click events emit nothing
- Given the unit tests run with a mocked input plugin, then they pass without Phaser


## Scope
- In scope: new game/frontend/src/phaser/input.ts
- In scope: unit tests in game/frontend/tests
- Out of scope: switching BootScene or React components to the layer (SG-3.3)
- Out of scope: new events beyond those in events.ts
- Out of scope: backend/
- Preserve: BootScene behaviour unchanged
- Preserve: events.ts event maps
- Preserve: Phaser ~3.90.0 pin


## Technical constraints
- Phaser stays pinned at ~3.90.0; phaser-pin guard test keeps passing
- No change to what the player sees or can do
- npm test and npm run typecheck pass in game/ and game/frontend/
- No source file over 200 lines
- game/src never imports from game/frontend
- Zustand store is the only owner of GameState
- No test deleted or skipped; tests mock only what is external


## Dependencies
- SG-3.1 typed bridge (done)


## Definition of done
- input.ts exists and is covered by unit tests
- All hard constraints hold


## Non-functional requirements
- No per-frame allocations; listeners released on destroy


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Input layer owns object focus and moveFocus and reports focusChange
nodes.body:
Context: BootScene.onKeyDown calls moveFocus, reads the focused id, writes useGameStore.setFocusedObject and emits focusChange. Desired behavior: createInputLayer exposes moveFocus(delta), focusObject(id) and focusedId() doing the same. Expected result: focus movement is testable without BootScene.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given three visible objects and none focused, when moveFocus(1) is called, then the first object is focused, store focusedObjectId is its id and focusChange is emitted with that id
- Given an object is focused, when focusObject(null) is called, then every object is blurred, store focus is null and focusChange emits {id:null}
- Given the first object is focused, when moveFocus(-1) is called, then focus wraps to the last visible object


## Scope
- In scope: createInputLayer, moveFocus, focusObject, focusedId in input.ts
- Out of scope: BootScene wiring
- Preserve: moveFocus in game/src/engine/buildScene.ts
- Preserve: gameStore.setFocusedObject


## Technical constraints
- Hard constraints of the intent apply (Phaser ~3.90.0, 200-line limit, game/src never imports game/frontend, Zustand owns state)


## Dependencies
- game/src/engine/buildScene.ts moveFocus
- game/frontend/src/store/gameStore.ts


## Definition of done
- Focus API works and emits focusChange


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Input layer maps Tab, arrows, Enter, Space and Escape to focus, interaction and menuClose
nodes.body:
Context: BootScene.onKeyDown (L177-L192) maps Tab/Shift+Tab/arrows to focus, Enter/Space to handleKey and Escape to menuClose. Desired behavior: createInputLayer registers that one keydown listener on input.keyboard.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given the layer, when Tab, ArrowRight or ArrowDown is pressed, then moveFocus(1) runs and preventDefault is called; Shift+Tab, ArrowLeft, ArrowUp move -1
- Given a focused object, when Enter or Space is pressed, then that object's handleKey is called with the key
- Given any state, when Escape is pressed, then menuClose is emitted with {}
- Given keyboard is undefined, then createInputLayer does not throw


## Scope
- In scope: keydown handler and registration in input.ts
- Out of scope: BootScene wiring
- Preserve: SceneObject.handleKey semantics


## Technical constraints
- Hard constraints of the intent apply


## Dependencies
- R1 focus API in the same file


## Definition of done
- All five key paths behave as in BootScene today


## Non-functional requirements
- Handler is a stable function; no per-keypress allocations beyond the event


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Input layer reports hover and click and removes every listener on destroy
nodes.body:
Context: BootScene.create binds o.onInteract to objectClick and o.onHoverChange to objectHover. Desired behavior: the layer binds these for every object and destroy() releases them and the keydown listener.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given an object, when its interact callback fires, then objectClick is emitted with its id
- Given an object, when hover starts then objectHover emits its id, and when hover ends it emits {id:null}
- Given destroy() was called, when key, hover or click callbacks fire, then no bridge event is emitted and keyboard.off was called with the registered handler
- Given destroy() is called twice, then the second call is a no-op


## Scope
- In scope: hover/click binding and destroy in input.ts
- Out of scope: character sprite clicks
- Out of scope: BootScene wiring
- Preserve: SceneObject.onInteract and onHoverChange API


## Technical constraints
- Hard constraints of the intent apply


## Dependencies
- R1, R2 in the same file


## Definition of done
- Hover, click and teardown covered


## Non-functional requirements
- All listeners released on destroy


## Clarifying questions
- None

steps.action: Create the file with imports of moveFocus from '@game/engine/buildScene', type SceneObject from '@game/entities/SceneObject', useGameStore from '../store/gameStore', phaserToReact from './events'. Declare the three types.

Export createInputLayer(input: InputPlugin, objects: SceneObject[]): InputLayer. Add focusedId() returning objects.find(o => o.isFocused)?.spec.id ?? null; a private report() that reads focusedId(), calls useGameStore.getState().setFocusedObject(id) and phaserToReact.emit('focusChange', { id }) and returns id; moveFocus(delta) calls moveFocus(objects, delta) then report(); focusObject(id) calls o.focus() on the object whose spec.id === id and o.blur() on every other (blur all when id is null) then report(). destroy() is a stub returning void for now.
steps.expected: Focus methods return the focused id and emit focusChange

steps.lines: after the focus methods in createInputLayer
steps.action: Add const onKeyDown = (e: KeyboardEvent): void with the same delta computation as BootScene.ts L178: Tab -> shiftKey ? -1 : 1; ArrowRight/ArrowDown -> 1; ArrowLeft/ArrowUp -> -1; else 0. If delta !== 0: e.preventDefault() and layer moveFocus(delta). Else if key is 'Enter' or ' ': objects.forEach(o => o.handleKey(e.key)). Else if 'Escape': phaserToReact.emit('menuClose', {}).
steps.code: if (delta !== 0) { e.preventDefault(); moveFocusBy(delta as 1 | -1); } else if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ') objects.forEach((o) => o.handleKey(e.key)); else if (e.key === 'Escape') phaserToReact.emit('menuClose', {});

steps.action: Call input.keyboard?.on('keydown', onKeyDown) once at construction.
steps.expected: One keydown listener registered; no throw when keyboard is undefined

steps.action: Add let active = true. For each object o call o.onInteract(e => { if (active) phaserToReact.emit('objectClick', { id: e.objectId }); }) and o.onHoverChange(e => { if (active) phaserToReact.emit('objectHover', { id: e.over ? e.objectId : null }); }).
steps.expected: Click and hover are emitted through the bridge only while active

steps.action: Implement destroy(): if (!active) return; active = false; input.keyboard?.off('keydown', onKeyDown).
steps.expected: Listener removed once; second call no-op

steps.action: Build a fake input {keyboard:{on:vi.fn(),off:vi.fn()}} and 3 fake objects with isVisible true, focus()/blur() setting isFocused, spec.id 'a','b','c', handleKey/onInteract/onHoverChange vi.fn().
